_comment: External exposure estimates for Views 6 and 7. These are NOT in the US Accidents dataset; each comes from a cited outside source. Shares are fractions of vehicle-miles (or of hours, where stated).

night.label: night
night.interval_note: Both sources give a single value of about 25%. The 22 to 28% band is a sensitivity range I set, not a published interval.
night.measure: share of vehicle-miles travelled during darkness

sources.quote: only 25 percent of vehicle miles traveled (VMT) occur at night

sources.short: Varghese and Shankar, NHTSA Research Note DOT HS 810 637 (2007)
sources.quote: approximately 25 percent of travel occurs during hours of darkness

night.context: NHTSA and FHWA report the nighttime fatality rate per mile at about three times the daytime rate. That is fatalities, not all reported incidents, so it is context rather than a check.

wet.label: rain
wet.interval_note: Range across the Missouri and Pennsylvania stations in Harwood et al. (8.3% Kansas City to 12.9% St. Louis); the midpoint is used as the central value. The same study finds 3.7% (Key West) to 38.5% (Washington rain forest) across climates, so no single national figure exists.
wet.measure: share of hours with wet pavement (WETTIME model, hourly weather records)
wet.measure_mismatch: Wet-pavement hours include drying time after rain stops, so they exceed hours when rain is falling. This project classifies a crash as wet when rain is reported falling, so the true exposure for that definition is lower than this estimate, which biases the computed rain rate downward.

sources.short: Harwood, Blackburn, Kibler and Kulakowski, Estimation of Wet Pavement Exposure from Available Weather Records, Transportation Research Record 1172 (1988), 32-41

independent_check.short: Qiu and Nixon, Effects of Adverse Weather on Traffic Crashes: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis, Transportation Research Record 2055 (2008), 139-146
independent_check.note: Rain increases the crash rate by 71% (95% CI 31 to 111%), pooled across studies that measured exposure directly.

fhwa_weather.short: FHWA Road Weather Management Program, How Do Weather Events Impact Roads? (2019-2023 averages of NHTSA data)
